text:
Nina: Proposal: move quota accounting to a write-ahead "ledger" stream (kafka) + a fairness scheduler that subscribes and emits admit decisions. Rationale: simpler cross-region consistency and easier audits. Thoughts?

Tom: Nice for audits but worried about critical path. Every admit hitting kafka before decision = added latency.

Jorge: We don't need strict sync. Pattern: edge does local fast-path using local counters, publishes a delta to ledger async. Scheduler consumes and computes corrective credits. Edges reconcile when they get updated credits.

Maya: That implies eventual consistency. How do we avoid thundering replays where many edges try to reclaim credits at once?

Nina: We shape credits as leases with expiry and small heartbeat renewals. Edges hold lease n tokens for T seconds. If they exceed, local soft-shed until reconciliation.

Tom: Lease model sketch: lease = {client_id, tokens, expires_at, version}. Edge admits from lease until tokens exhausted, then consult scheduler/central for refill.

Jorge: Important: fairness decisions are global, so scheduler should run periodic rebalancer windows (eg 1s or 5s) and produce per-client adjustments. It writes adjustments back to ledger topic; edges subscribe to adjustment stream.

Maya: What about abusive clients trying to request new leases fast? Need anti-abuse controls in both edge and scheduler. Edge enforces rate-limited lease requests and scheduler enforces backpressure per client fingerprint.

Nina: Also propose a short-circuit for emergencies: a small central admission API for high-tail checks (p95 p99) where edge asks synchronously if it has "hot" suspicion. That keeps common path local.

Tom: Good. Need clear invariants: 1) no admit that violates last-known global negative balance beyond some epsilon. 2) leases are conservative by default.

Jorge: Migration plan: 1) implement ledger producer in edges (emit deltas), 2) read-only simulator of scheduler in staging to validate rebalances, 3) issue leases from scheduler but keep tokenbank in parallel for a period, 4) cutover when divergence < threshold.

Maya: Telemetry: emit lease_granted, lease_used, fallback_local_admits, ledger_lag_ms, scheduler_apply_latency. Sample high-traffic clients fully.

Nina: API/contract: ledger record types: DELTA (client_id, delta_tokens, prefix_hash, ts), LEASE (client_id, tokens, expiry, version), ADJUST (client_id, delta, reason, policy_version). Keep record schema compact to reduce bandwidth.

Tom: For privacy/Private deployments we must support running ledger inside customer VPC or allow edges to keep full local policy and only send hashed features.

Jorge: Abuse signals: scheduler maintains per-fingerprint abuse score and can revoke leases by publishing ADJUST with negative delta + notice. Edges should apply revocations immediately on receipt.

Maya: Failure modes: if scheduler down, edges fallback to tokenbucket local with conservative refill. ops-bot should raise if ledger consumer lag > 10s or ADJUST apply failed rate > 0.5%.

ops-bot: :warning: Suggested alert - ledger_consumer_lag_1m > 10s OR adjust_apply_error_rate_5m > 0.5% -> Pager. (playbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/ledger-failures)

Nina: Pricing / perf tradeoffs: extra infra but benefits: consistent fairness, simpler audits, easier per-tenant backfills.

Tom: Implementation details: use compacted topic for LEASE and ADJUST, use non-compacted for DELTA. Key by client_id or sharded prefix depending on cardinality.

Jorge: For high-cardinality prefixes we'll shard by prefix_hash % N and use local partial aggregates at edges to reduce delta churn.

Maya: Security: sign ledger records or use mTLS between producers/consumers. Also rotation for keys and RBAC on topics.

Nina: Next steps: I'll draft RFC with schema, simulator plan, and rollout checklist. Can owners volunteer for prototype?

Tom: I'll do the staging simulator + latency tests.

Jorge: I'll own the scheduler prototype and rebalancer algorithm.

Maya: I'll add telemetry and ops alerting.

Nina: Great. Target RFC by next Tue. Please add notes to PR and tag owners. Thanks :+1:
